## Detailed entries

### Ashland

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Date enacted:** 2026-02-26 per a WSAZ headline ("Ordinance passed for data center applications"); this reads as the initial temporary moratorium, later replaced before its natural expiration by a permanent zoning ordinance given first/second readings on 2026-07-23/2026-07-24
- **Normalized date:** `2026-02-26` (unverified)
- **Duration:** Reported as roughly 6 months; superseded before expiration by a permanent conditional-use zoning ordinance
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ky-ashland-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Temporary City Commission moratorium ordinance (Boyd County); ordinance number not located in sources reviewed
- **What prompted it:** Rubix Data Centers' proposed roughly 2-gigawatt data center campus near the former Ashland steel mill site prompted the Commission to pause new applications to study zoning ordinances
- **Affected projects:** Rubix Data Centers' proposed ~2 GW data center campus near the former Ashland steel mill site
- **Detailed status:** Replaced. A July 25, 2026 news account describes Ashland as having been "under a moratorium for the construction and operation of data centers" for "the last five-plus months," superseded when the City Commission passed permanent conditional-use zoning restrictions (I-2 heavy-industrial only, 1,500-ft residential setback, 50,000 sq ft cap, 45-ft height limit, 55dB noise limit, water-use cap) on first and second readings 2026-07-23/24, before the moratorium's own term would have lapsed. [VERIFY instrument number; primary source (news-only evidence) not confirmed at confidence 0.55 in the 2026-07 refresh]
- **Outcome:** Temporary moratorium adopted, then superseded by a permanent conditional-use zoning ordinance

### City of La Grange

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** ⚪ Expired
- **Date enacted:** 2025-06-02
- **Normalized date:** `2025-06-02` (exact)
- **Duration:** 150 days initially; extension ordinance identified but final term needs confirmation
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ky-la-grange-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance No. 10, Series 2025; Ordinance No. 17-2025 listed as "An Ordinance Extending Moratorium"
- **What prompted it:** Increased data center interest in Oldham County; infrastructure, energy, land-use, environmental, and regulatory-gap concerns
- **Affected projects:** Project Lincoln / OC Data Center area proposals; new applications paused, filed applications exempted
- **Detailed status:** Ordinance 17-2025 extended the moratorium by 150 days, approved unanimously at the City Council's meeting reported November 10, 2025 (the prior moratorium had expired October 30, 2025 per the ordinance). That places the extension's own computed term at roughly early-to-mid April 2026. The City of La Grange's official ordinance index (lagrangeky.gov/ordinances, checked 2026-07-31 and current through ordinances dated late June 2026) lists 2026 ordinances 01, 02, 05, 07, and 09 through 13 -- covering code-enforcement duties, a zoning map amendment, sign regulations, an annexation, and FY2026-27 budgets -- with no ordinance addressing data centers, a further moratorium extension, or permanent data-center zoning regulations. No City Council action on data centers has been identified since Ordinance 17-2025.
- **Outcome:** The 150-day extension (Ordinance 17-2025) has run its course (computed term ending roughly April 2026) with no further extension or permanent replacement ordinance appearing in the city's own current ordinance index through late June 2026, indicating the moratorium has lapsed on its own terms.

### Oldham County Fiscal Court

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2025-06-26 (per Oldham Era public notice scheduling second reading/public hearing/adoption for that date); signed-ordinance date with vote tally not separately retrieved [VERIFY: signed ordinance copy with vote tally not retrieved as of 2026-04-29]
- **Normalized date:** `2025-06-26` (unverified)
- **Duration:** 150 days initially; later extended until data center regulations are approved
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ky-oldham-county-fiscal-court-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance KOC 25-910-508; extension KOC 25-910-520
- **What prompted it:** Increased data center siting interest; infrastructure, utility capacity, energy use, land use, and environmental sustainability concerns; zoning rules did not adequately address data centers
- **Affected projects:** Project Lincoln / OC Data Center proposal near La Grange; reporting describes a withdrawn proposal after intense public pushback
- **Detailed status:** Still in effect as of 2026-07-31. The Oldham County Planning & Zoning Commission voted unanimously on 2026-06-23 to forward revised zoning text amendments to the Fiscal Court. The Fiscal Court held a first reading of the resulting ordinance (KOC 26-920-5, 'zoning text amendments of the comprehensive zoning ordinance') at a special meeting on 2026-06-29, per the Court's own posted agenda. A closed session on pending/proposed litigation was held 2026-07-14 (subject not specified on the public agenda). A second reading of KOC 26-920-5 was calendared for the Fiscal Court's 2026-07-21 meeting per the Court's own posted agenda. As of this research date, no signed minutes confirming the outcome of that July 21 second reading had been posted publicly, so whether KOC 26-920-5 has been finally adopted -- which would likely supersede the moratorium -- remains unconfirmed.
- **Outcome:** After the January 2026 remand, the Planning & Zoning Commission's revised regulations reached the Fiscal Court as KOC 26-920-5, with first reading 2026-06-29 and second reading calendared 2026-07-21. Passage of second reading was not confirmed in public records as of 2026-07-31; the moratorium (KOC 25-910-508, extended by KOC 25-910-520 'until data center regulations are approved') remains the best-supported operative instrument pending that confirmation.
